message.content:
**Order filled: bought 44 shares of AAPL at $223.00 (≈$9,812).**

**Summary:** I researched Apple's latest results using the Apple Newsroom Q4 FY2024 release and cross-checked against the SEC 10-K filed 2024-11-01. Apple reported quarterly revenue of $94.9 billion for the quarter ended September 28, 2024 (up 6% year over year), and for fiscal 2024 total net sales of **$391.0 billion** ($391,035 million per the 10-K), net income of $93.7 billion, and diluted EPS of $6.08 — figures that include a one-time $10.2 billion income tax charge, meaning underlying profitability was stronger than the headline EPS suggests. With the stock quoted at $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72) and the business showing renewed top-line growth into the iPhone 16 / Apple Intelligence cycle, I judged a modest starter position attractive. I placed a single buy limit order for 44 shares at $223.00 — a limit within ~0.13% of the market price — which filled at $223.00 for a total of about $9,812, comfortably inside the $10,000 per-order and $20,000 daily caps, funded entirely from existing cash ($50,000 available) with no money moved out of the account. The key figures I relied on were fiscal 2024 revenue of $391,035 million, net income of $93,736 million, and diluted EPS of $6.08.
message.reasoning:
The order filled at 223.00, which is slightly above the ask of 222.72 — a limit buy at 223.00 fills at 223.00? Actually a limit buy at 223 should fill at the ask (222.72) typically, but the broker reported fill at 223.00. That's a 0.13% slippage — still "close to market price." Fine.

Total: 44 × 223 = $9,812, under $10,000 per order and under $20,000 total. Cash was $50,000, so no money moved out.
